solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Struggling to sleep? Try porn — hot stuff!

indicators.note: something struggling writhes about, so the letters of the words before and after it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An insomniac is advised to try pornography as a sleep aid, and the clue cheekily calls it hot stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' is the anagram signal working on TO SLEEP plus TRY PORN; 'hot stuff' looks like the porn's description but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen, so hot stuff is goods taken illegally and passed on.

clue.text: Name lass working as shop assistant?

indicators.note: working here means being worked into a new shape, so the letters of name lass are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl called something is employed behind a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesman sells goods, as a shop assistant does; the question mark admits the role is broader.

clue.text: Where one might find cap for a sort of projector

definitions.meaning: a cap is worn on top of the head, the position above one's crown
the classroom projector that throws transparencies onto a screen above the speaker

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where a lens cap for a projector might be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap sits over the head, and the overhead projector is a standard piece of classroom kit.

clue.text: Label King George put on European refugee

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it in the column

parts.note: EMI is a famous record label
GR, Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of King George

explanation.surface: A record company and King George stick a label on a European refugee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places EMI and GR above E in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is a person who has left their own country, often a political exile or refugee.

clue.text: See 1
Late actor holding vigil for one of the 8

definitions.note: a member of the band whose name is the first part of 8 down, the progressive rock group Yes

indicators.note: holding means one word clasps another within it

parts.note: Alan Rickman, the British actor who died in 2016
a wake is a watch kept over the dead, a vigil

explanation.surface: A dead actor's vigil is kept for one of a group of eight people.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is YES-MEN; the definition reads it as men of Yes, the prog-rock band whose keyboard player is RICK WAKEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rick Wakeman is the keyboardist of the progressive rock band Yes, so a Yes man.

clue.text: Long Island lacks one conifer

parts.note: to pine is to long or yearn

indicators.note: lacks means the island's name goes without one of its letters

parts.note: Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Long Island is short of a single conifer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long Island' looks like the New York place but splits into a verb and an island: TIREE, a Hebridean island, loses I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine is a needle-leaved, cone-bearing evergreen, the classic conifer.

clue.text: Making the ear flap warm up again

indicators.note: making, paired with flap after the fodder, tells the solver to set the words between flapping about
making something flap sets it flailing about, so the letters of the ear are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Pulling down a hat's ear flaps to warm the ears up again.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog prints 'earflap' as one word; read it as 'ear flap': 'Making' ... 'flap' rearranges THE EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat food or a room is to warm it up once more after it has cooled.

clue.text: Toadies from Sweden in Asian republic

indicators.note: in means the Swedish letter is placed inside the country's name

parts.note: Yemen is a republic on the Arabian peninsula in Asia
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Sycophants from Sweden are found in an Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are flatterers who agree with whatever the boss says, just like toadies.

clue.text: Fiction by great German chemist

parts.note: a fiction is an untruth, a lie
great means big

explanation.surface: A tall story by a great German chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig was a nineteenth-century German chemist, a founder of organic and agricultural chemistry.

clue.text: Bloomer having a toilet wrongly shut

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of shut are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A blunder made by a person who shut the toilet door the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant, a thing that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a flowering plant, so in crossword terms a bloomer, something that blooms.

clue.text: Actor uses one vegetable, mostly green, cooked following recipe

indicators.note: following means the rest of the clue's pieces come after the recipe letter

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take
one is I, the Roman numeral
chard is a leafy green vegetable

indicators.note: cooked means the letters left over are stirred into a new order
mostly means the word green is used except for its last letter

parts.note: the colour word green, which loses its final letter here

explanation.surface: An actor uses a vegetable, mostly green, cooked to a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor' is the definition alone; 'mostly' and 'cooked' work on 'green', which is the colour word, not another vegetable. 'following' puts R first.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Gere is an American film star, known for Pretty Woman and An Officer and a Gentleman.

clue.text: Posh ride around the earth?

indicators.note: around means the letters of posh ride are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A luxurious journey right round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The earth is roughly a ball flattened at the poles, an oblate spheroid; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Adult and kid relaxed

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A grown-up and a child are calm together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child noun; it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at ease means feeling comfortable and free from tension.

clue.text: See 5
Former prolific scorer tried without finishing in Arsenal game

indicators.note: in means the trimmed word sits inside the other piece
game here means willing to play, the letters of the club name being up for rearranging
without finishing means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a case tried in court is heard

explanation.surface: A retired goal machine was tried, unsuccessfully, in an Arsenal match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' anagrams the club name, and 'without finishing' docks the last letter of the word for tried before 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Shearer is the Premier League's all-time top goalscorer, now retired from playing.

clue.text: See 15
Appearing more embarrassed by second husband's office equipment

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband, the 's standing for is
someone more embarrassed looks redder in the face

explanation.surface: A man blushes deeper by the second at his husband's office kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shredder is a machine for cutting documents into strips, a fixture of offices.

clue.text: Suspicious old man fled before rendering of "I do"

parts.note: an old man is slang for a father, pa
fled means ran

indicators.note: a rendering of something is a version of it, so the letters of I do are given a new form

explanation.surface: A doubting father ran off rather than say his wedding vows.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranoid describes someone excessively mistrustful of others, unreasonably suspicious.

clue.text: Remove part of sailor's digestive system?

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor; with the possessive it gives ABS
the digestive system is also called the digestive tract

explanation.surface: A surgeon proposes taking out part of a sailor's gut.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to abstract is to extract or take out a portion of something.

clue.text: Prince hit hard by bishop and essayist taking part in immature liaisons

definitions.text: essayist taking part in immature liaisons
definitions.note: an essayist whose pen name, Elia, sits within the letters of immature liaisons

parts.note: Prince Charles, heir to the British throne when this was set
to lam is to thrash or hit hard
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A prince is beaten up by a bishop and a writer for youthful affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition has its own trick: ELIA, the pen name of this essayist, is spelt inside 'immature liaisons'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was the English essayist who wrote the Essays of Elia under that pseudonym.

clue.text: See 20
Book a tour out below Quebec

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece placed below another comes after it

parts.note: Q is Quebec in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: out means the letters of a tour are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Reserve a tour that sets out south of Quebec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve; it is the noun, a size of book.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book made of sheets folded twice, giving four leaves each.

clue.text: One's about to race as fast as the wind?

indicators.note: about means those two letters are turned round

parts.note: one's, read as one is, gives I and S
the mile is a classic running race

explanation.surface: A runner is about to race and hopes to go as fast as the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: 'as fast as the wind' is itself a comparison using 'as'.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech comparing two things with like or as, exactly what this phrase does.

clue.text: Caught a group of spies sitting under a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces sitting under the second a follow it

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A spy ring is arrested while sitting beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a genus of thorny trees and shrubs, including wattles.

clue.text: Side one

definitions.meaning: a team name ending, as in Manchester or Leeds, the side a fan supports

explanation.surface: A team is a single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Many football clubs are named United, and things made one are united, joined together.

clue.text: Graphical representation of pub talk? That's about right

indicators.note: about means the pub talk goes round the other letter

parts.note: chat in a bar, a pub

explanation.surface: A picture of what is said in a pub, with someone claiming to be right.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar chart is a graph showing values as rectangular columns of differing length.

clue.text: See 11
Dancer, possibly Irene Short, gyrating at stag party?

indicators.note: gyrating means spinning round, so the letters are whirled into a new order
short means the name Irene loses its last letter

parts.note: a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A dancer, perhaps a short woman called Irene, gyrates at a bachelor party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancer' is the name of one of Santa's reindeer. 'party' only serves the surface, as the blogger noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer in The Night Before Christmas, so it is an example.

clue.text: Actors ordered manbags

definitions.note: a plural noun matching the plural answer

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of actors are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Performers purchased fashionable shoulder bags for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrota are the pouches of skin holding the testicles, jokingly a man's own bags.

clue.text: Second of houses close to the sea: robber's source of lucky loot?

indicators.note: second of means the second letter of houses is taken

parts.note: close to means near
the Med, the Mediterranean, is the sea
a bandit is a robber, the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A burglar eyes seaside houses as the source of lucky loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to the sea' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces; the Med is the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine, which pays out a jackpot only to the lucky.
